label: Purple needlegrass
taxonomy_note: Jepson currently uses Stipa pulchra; Nassella pulchra is a widely used alternate combination. No cultivar/local accession asserted.
seasonal_behavior: Cool/wet-season green bunchgrass; flowering fine purple-tinged awns, then straw dry-season blades/seedheads. Moisture alters dormancy and greenness; no generic tree leaf fall.

Using the supplied ChirpNeighbors plant sprite sheet ONLY as visual style/camera/light/pixel-density reference, create FOUR DIFFERENT new plant sprites, not the plants in that reference. Match its strong detailed naturalistic pixel art: visible crisp square pixel clusters, stepped edges, controlled organic palette, subtle outline and precise pixel shading. Warm upper-left light, three-quarter side garden view with slight top visibility. Not smooth illustration, photo, watercolor, 3D or UI. Quiet plant artwork supports birds as focus; no birds or animals.

TRUE transparent alpha. Exactly FOUR complete separated rooted plant sprites arranged in a 2 by 2 grid. Wide fully empty transparent gutters; every silhouette fits inside its own quadrant at no more than 74 percent cell width/height. At least 10 percent empty transparent margins on ALL sides of each plant. No touching frame, no cropped leaves or seeds, no overlap, no labels/text/panels/checkerboard/backdrop. No pots or ground tiles. Each natural base has just a few tiny contact pebbles. Fit each plant independently; cell sizes do not imply physical scale.

UPPER LEFT — Purple needlegrass, Stipa pulchra (Nassella pulchra): one natural fine-leaved bunchgrass tuft, thin arching green blades with a little straw at the basal crown. Several slender airy upright flowering/seed culms carrying long fine PURPLE-TINGED NEEDLE AWNS in open sparse panicles. Delicate fine awns extending fully inside frame, no purple flowers, no thick wheat ears, no huge feathery pampas plumes. Healthy cool-season green state with subtle early seed awns.
UPPER RIGHT — Blue-eyed grass, Sisyrinchium bellum: low compact iris-family clump with narrow flat swordlike green blades, several thin stems carrying SMALL VIOLET BLUE SIX-TEPALED STAR FLOWERS WITH GOLDEN YELLOW CENTERS. Clearly tiny blue-eyed-grass flowers above grasslike leaves, not large bearded irises or five-petaled daisies. Healthy spring flowering state.
LOWER LEFT — California poppy, Eschscholzia californica: delicate low airy clump of finely divided glaucous blue-green leaves, slender upright curving stems with golden-orange CUP FLOWERS made of FOUR smooth silky petals. A few tapered buds and one thin young seed pod, no black central blotch, no red opium poppy, no ruffled double cultivar. Healthy orange-flowering phenotype, local cultivar/subtaxon identity not asserted.
LOWER RIGHT — Shaw's agave, Agave shawii: ONE NONFLOWERING healthy compact green succulent ROSETTE with thick broad upward-curving glossy green leaves, reddish-brown sharp marginal teeth and brown terminal spines. Leaves form dense bowl-shaped upright coastal agave form, not long blue chalk agave, not aloe spots and not yucca narrow grass. NO tall flower stalk, no annual flowering. Entire tips/spines/root collar visible. Restricted coastal southern California species context, not generic desert-yard filler.

Four separate flattened whole sprites, no independently separated foliage/stem layers implied. Pixel art must remain detailed, natural and readable at game scale.
